original_question: In Theorem 8, one assumes a function psi(t) that increases to infinity and then constructs real numbers theta_1, theta_2, eta_1, eta_2 with inf_{x in Z_+} x psi(x) ||x theta_1 - eta_1|| ||x theta_2 - eta_2|| > 0. Can the same conclusion still hold when psi(t) is the positive constant psi_0 for all t, rather than a function tending to infinity? If not, the paper notes that this would imply a stronger inhomogeneous version of Littlewood's conjecture.
target_in_paper: The open problem stated immediately after Theorem 8 in Section 1, asking whether the conclusion of Theorem 8 still holds when the auxiliary function psi is replaced by a positive constant.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right local target in the paper: the question posed right after Theorem 8, concerning whether the loss factor psi(t) tending to infinity can be removed and replaced by a constant. It also correctly captures the conclusion sought, namely the existence of real shifts eta_1, eta_2 and real numbers theta_1, theta_2 for which x psi(x) ||x theta_1 - eta_1|| ||x theta_2 - eta_2|| stays bounded away from 0 on positive integers x, and it correctly notes the paper's comment that a negative answer would yield a stronger inhomogeneous Littlewood-type statement.
missing_details: Theorem 8 assumes more than monotone divergence of psi(t): besides psi(t) -> +infinity, it also requires the regularity condition sup_{x >= 1} psi(wx)/psi(x) < +infinity for every w >= 1.
The numbers theta_1 and theta_2 in Theorem 8 are required to be linearly independent over Z together with 1.
The norm notation ||·|| should be defined explicitly as distance to the nearest integer.
The infimum is taken over positive integers x in Z_+.
The constant-function variant should specify psi(t) = psi_0 > 0 for all t.
To make the question stand alone, it helps to say explicitly that it asks whether the exact conclusion of Theorem 8 survives after removing the factor tending to infinity.

Nearby context matters: Theorem 7 gives the corresponding constant-factor lower bound in the linearly dependent-with-1 case, so the open problem is specifically about whether the same phenomenon can occur in the linearly independent-with-1 case.
The phrase about a 'stronger inhomogeneous version of Littlewood's conjecture' is context supplied by the paper, not the formal statement of the problem itself.
refined_question: Let ||·|| denote distance to the nearest integer. Theorem 8 states that if psi:[1,∞)->(0,∞) is increasing, satisfies psi(t)->+infinity as t->+infinity, and for every w >= 1 obeys sup_{x >= 1} psi(wx)/psi(x) < +infinity, then there exist real numbers theta_1, theta_2 that are linearly independent over Z together with 1, and real numbers eta_1, eta_2, such that inf_{x in Z_+} x psi(x) ||x theta_1 - eta_1|| ||x theta_2 - eta_2|| > 0. Does this conclusion remain true when psi is replaced by a positive constant function psi(t) = psi_0 > 0 for all t?
justification: The draft is targeting not a broader Littlewood-type problem, nor Harrap's later question, but the specific open problem posed immediately after Theorem 8. The paper first records Theorem 7, which gives an inhomogeneous lower bound of the form inf_{x in Z_+} x ||x theta_1 - eta_1|| ||x theta_2 - eta_2|| > 0 when theta_1, theta_2 are linearly dependent over Z together with 1; then Theorem 8 proves an analogous statement in the linearly independent case, but only with an extra factor psi(x) tending to infinity and satisfying a mild multiplicative regularity condition. The author then asks exactly whether Theorem 8 still holds for constant psi, and remarks that otherwise one would obtain a stronger inhomogeneous Littlewood-type statement. So your draft is very close, but it omits the regularity assumption on psi, the linear independence condition with 1, and the precise scope of the positive-integer infimum.
